title: Tucker expert bank + Mirror expert coefficients
hypothesis: A shared Tucker matrix bank plus a compact Mirror address can represent many routed logical experts at lower total bytes than free Tucker expert coefficients, while preserving top-1 routed outputs; generic PCA and independent experts are controls.
physical_object: shared bank of K=8 matrices of shape 16x16 for E=128 logical experts
mirror_coordinate: one shared 8-vector and one Givens angle per expert
logical_multiplicity: 128 expert functions under deterministic balanced top-1 dispatch

model.dispatch: fixed balanced cyclic hash, identical across methods

controls: Tucker bank plus free expert coefficients
shared Mirror vector plus per-expert Givens angle

development.selection_metric: routed output NRMSE, expert matrix NRMSE, actual payload bytes and materialization compute

paid_objects: independent matrices or expert coefficients/factors fp16
storage.router: fixed balanced hash; no learned router state

success_gate: Aligned routed output NRMSE <=0.01 and >=20% fewer bytes than free Tucker expert coefficients; generic PCA matching Mirror means no Mirror-specific result. Independent coefficients test need for private experts.
failure_gate: Mirror misses quality/byte gate or generic PCA matches/improves Mirror; independent coefficients requiring free expert state are the capacity boundary.
boundaries: Fixed dispatch; no learned router or load balancing optimization
Aligned experts generated from the same Givens family
No language-model or MoE training evidence
